title: add downgrade guard + backup/restore + schema migrations for private-installer
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Add downgrade prevention guard for private installer upgrades; include safe backup/restore hooks and pg schema migration checks. No customer-facing API changes. Ops-runbook updated.
body:
Motivation:
This PR adds guards and automation to make Private installer upgrades safer for on-prem and VPC customers. In the past customers have hit irrecoverable state after partial upgrades or when downgrading across schema-changing releases. This change introduces a downgrade-guard check, baked-in backup/restore hooks, and a safer schema migration strategy for Postgres-backed control plane components.

What this changes (summary):
- Add a downgrade guard that prevents applying a release with a lower pinned component version unless a explicit --force-downgrade flag is set and backup present
- Wire pre-upgrade backup and post-upgrade verification steps into the private-installer CLI and Helm chart hooks
- Introduce idempotent schema migration runner with explicit migration metadata (version, checksum) and dry-run mode for validation
- Add Terraform module outputs to record current pinned versions to aid automated rollbacks
- Update upgrade runbook with step-by-step recoveries and verification commands

Checklist:
- [x] CLI: preflight checks and --force-downgrade flag
- [x] Helm: pre-upgrade/post-upgrade hooks for backups and verification
- [x] Terraform: outputs and state validation helpers
- [x] Database: migration runner with checksumed migrations and dry-run
- [x] Tests: unit tests for downgrade guard logic and integration test for backup/restore flow
- [x] Docs: runbook + upgrade verification steps

Commits (high-level):
- Add downgrade guard flag, validation logic and error messages
- Implement pre-upgrade backup hook (helm hook + installer shim)
- Post-upgrade verification: schema checksum compare, health checks, snapshot retention policy
- Add migration runner: checksum file, dry-run mode, validation endpoint
- Terraform: expose pinned_version output and add verify_version script
- Add unit and integration tests + CI job updates

Files changed (high-level):
- private-installer/cli/upgrade.go (new preflight and flags)
- private-installer/helm/charts/controlplane/templates/hooks.yaml (backup/verify hooks)
- private-installer/migrations/ (new migration runner + checksums)
- modules/terraform/private-installer/main.tf (outputs + verify script)
- docs/private-installer/upgrade-runbook.md (updated runbook)
- test/integration/upgrade_backup_restore_test.go (integration test)

Testing and CI:
- Added unit tests for downgrade guard logic (covers pinned-version comparisons and --force-downgrade flow).
- Integration test spins up a local Postgres (testcontainer), applies a migration, simulates upgrade/downgrade, runs backup, then verifies restore idempotency.
- CI initially failed linting for missing comments on exported functions; fixed in follow-up commit. All CI checks passing on merge.

Review notes and rationale:
- Downgrade guard semantics are intentionally conservative: default is to block any head_branch whose resolved component pins are older than the current deployed pins. The operator must either provide an explicit --force-downgrade and a verified backup, or perform a manual rollback following runbook steps. This reduces customer risk from accidental downgrades.
- Migration runner stores a small metadata record in the control-plane DB to mark applied migration version and checksum; this avoids re-running migrations that are already applied and allows verification after restore.
- Helm hooks are best-effort and non-blocking in truly air-gapped environments; the installer shim will run the same hooks when Helm hooks are not supported.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: long-running backups may extend upgrade window. Mitigation: backups are configurable (full vs logical) and operators can opt-in to quick snapshot + logical incremental strategy; we default to logical + validation to minimize downstream drift.
- Risk: consumers with custom migration steps might be disrupted. Mitigation: dry-run mode and explicit migration manifests give operators a way to test locally before applying.

Related linear/jira:
- ENG-5473 (upgrade safety initiative)

implement pre-upgrade backup hook and post-upgrade verification

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Important improvement. Left inline comments around the checksum storage format and retention policy - prefer TTL on migration metadata rather than indefinite retention.
Priya Nair: Reply: migrated metadata will include applied_at and optional ttl; updated migration runner to accept --retention-days and default to 90 days for metadata cleanup.
Lena Hsu: Can we ensure Helm hooks are no-op in air-gapped environments? Left a suggestion to add an installer shim fallback.
Priya Nair: Reply: added installer shim and tests for the shim path. Also extended integration test to run without Helm (simulating air-gapped ops).
Samir Patel: Approving after minor nits were fixed (naming and an exported comment). CI passing.
